title: Runtime meta-scheduler for dual-path attention kernels with short-horizon prefill probing
creator: Sofia Chen
description:
Summary:
We need a low-risk runtime meta-scheduler that chooses between two classes of attention kernels (prefill-optimized and decode-optimized) on a per-session basis. The scheduler must make fast, explainable decisions using short-horizon probes during session warmup, match kernel to hardware/sequence-length profile, and support safe regret-bounded swaps at decode time if the chosen kernel underperforms.

Background and motivation:
- Our serving runtime currently selects kernels via static heuristics based on GPU architecture and average sequence length. This fails for mixed workloads: some sessions have long-prefill bursts followed by short decode, others have unpredictable prefill lengths.
- Choosing the wrong attention implementation increases p95 latency, reduces throughput, and harms cost-efficiency. We need a light-weight online policy that adapts to per-session signals without adding heavy overhead.

Goals (measurable):
- Reduce median tokens-per-dollar for mixed workloads by at least 8% vs baseline across production traces.
- Keep user-visible regressions below 1.5% (latency or quality) and p95 latency change <= +5% on safety guardrails.
- Probe overhead: additional latency during warmup must be <= 10ms per probe on average and <= 50ms worst-case for first 5 requests.

High-level approach:
1) Hardware & session fingerprinting: collect GPU family, SM count, memory bandwidth, and early session stats (first 8–16 token lengths, token arrival rate, past model variant if known).
2) Short-horizon prefill probes: for a new session, run 2–6 micro-probes that execute a minimal forward with candidate kernels using short prefix inputs. Record latency, occupancy, and KV-cache behavior. Probes run asynchronously and time-boxed.
3) Cost/regret model: compute a lightweight estimated cost surface (latency per-token + resource multiplier) and pick the kernel with lowest expected regret over a short horizon. The model is a linear cost function learned offline from replay data, with architecture-dependent coefficients.
4) Regret-bounded swap policy: allow one swap mid-decode if a sliding-window of recent latency deviates beyond a threshold and the estimated improvement exceeds swap cost. Swaps must be safe: preserve deterministic outputs or fall back to model variants that maintain semantics.
5) Warm-start catalog: use offline fingerprints to seed decisions for known instance types (e.g., A100-40GB, H100-80GB) to avoid probes on common footprints.

Data & instrumentation plan:
- Add structured probe telemetry: probe_id, kernel_candidate, probe_latency_us, kv_cache_hit_ratio, sm_util_pct, active_batch_size.
- Log decision trace per session: fingerprint -> chosen_kernel -> post_deploy_metrics (p50/p95 latency, tokens/s).
- Add labels to existing dashboards (runtime-kernel-decisions) for per-customer and per-model aggregation.

Experimentation & validation:
- Offline replay: run probes and decision logic against 2 weeks of sampled production traces to validate expected cost surface and swap thresholds.
- Synthetic stress tests: create traces that flip prefill length mid-session and verify swap policy correctness and safety properties.
- Canary rollout: 1% traffic -> 5% -> 20% with continuous monitoring of latency, error rates, and cost. Auto-rollback if p95 regresses by >10% or error rate increases by >0.5%.

Success metrics and dashboards:
- Primary: tokens-per-dollar (aggregate), relative to baseline; target -8% improvement.
- Secondary: p50/p95 latency, median decode throughput, probe overhead (ms).
- Safety: swap count per 10k sessions, percentage of sessions that saw regression, error rates.

Rollout plan and controls:
- Feature flag gating per-customer (console + runtime switch).
- Canary rollout by region and hardware family.
- Kill-switch: global disable via runtime config for immediate rollback.

Risks and mitigation:
- Probe overhead amplifies cold-start latency: limit probes to the first N requests and cap worst-case latency; fall back to warm-start if host is in warm catalog.
- Swap correctness risks deterministic outputs: restrict swaps to kernels with compatible numerical paths or add checksum verification on small decode windows before finalizing swap.
- Model/Quality regressions: add automated evaluation with golden prompts in the canary stage.

Implementation milestones:
- Week 1: instrumentation schema + offline replay harness (Sofia + Marco).
- Week 2: probe executor + light cost model implementation (Marco).
- Week 3: swap policy + safety checks + unit tests (Marco + Liam).
- Week 4: canary rollout + dashboards + post-canary analysis (Sofia + Amina).

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Probe budget: 2 vs 6 probes — more probes yield better estimates but increase cold latency. Proposed default = 3 probes with exponential backoff.
- Swap frequency cap: allow at most 1 swap per session vs allow multiple but cost-accounted. Proposed: single swap per session to bound complexity.
- Learning components: fully online bandit vs offline linear cost model. We start offline + occasional bandit exploration; revisit after canary.
